cards.text: Jesus is in one of the towns when a man comes along covered with leprosy. Not a patch here and there. COVERED. When he sees Jesus, he falls facedown and begs Him.

cards.question: The man covered with leprosy is facedown in front of Jesus, begging. What is he asking for?

answers.text: For Jesus to make him clean
For Jesus to let him follow
For Jesus to pray for his family

cards.question: The man covered with leprosy isn't sure Jesus has the power to heal him.

cards.text: Jesus reaches out His hand and touches the man. TOUCHES him! I bet that man did not see that coming.

cards.question: The man said, "Lord, if You are willing." How does Jesus answer him?
Jesus says, "Be clean!" And the man's leprosy leaves him ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus gives the healed man some instructions. Friend, if that were me, I'd already be running down the street YELLING.

cards.question: Jesus tells the man He just healed of leprosy to go spread the word all over town.
Jesus tells the healed man to go show himself to the ___ and present the offering Moses prescribed for his cleansing.

cards.text: Jesus said don't tell anyone. And the news about Jesus spreads ALL the more. Friend, there is no such thing as "just between us."

cards.question: As the news about Jesus spreads, great crowds come. Why are they coming?

answers.text: To hear Him and be healed
To crown Him as their king
To see the man who was healed

cards.question: With great crowds coming to Jesus, He stops slipping away to the wilderness to pray.

cards.text: Another day, Jesus is teaching, and the Pharisees and teachers of the law, religious leaders of the day, are sitting right there. People have come from Jerusalem and from every village of Galilee and Judea.

cards.question: As Jesus teaches that day, the power of the Lord is present for Him to heal the sick.

cards.text: Just then some men show up carrying a paralyzed man on a mat. They want to get him inside and set him right in front of Jesus.

cards.question: The men carrying the paralyzed man try to get him inside to Jesus. What's in their way?
The men can't get the paralyzed man through the crowd, but they don't quit. They go up on the ___.
The men lower the paralyzed man on his mat through the tiles, and he lands at the back of the crowd.

cards.text: Friend, if the parking lot's full, I am going HOME. These men went through the ROOF. And Jesus sees it all.

cards.question: Jesus looks at the men who lowered the paralyzed man through the roof. What does He see in them?
The first thing Jesus says to the paralyzed man is that his sins are forgiven.

cards.text: I don't think that line goes over well with the scribes and Pharisees. Nobody says a word out loud, but they start thinking to themselves.

cards.question: The scribes and Pharisees think Jesus is speaking blasphemy. They ask themselves, "Who can forgive sins but ___ alone?"

cards.text: Jesus knows what they're thinking, and He asks why they're thinking these things in their hearts. That's typing about your boss in the group chat, then seeing your boss is IN the group chat.

cards.question: Jesus asks the scribes and Pharisees which is easier to say to the paralyzed man. "Your sins are forgiven" or what?

cards.text: Jesus calls Himself the Son of Man. And He's about to show everybody in that room something.

cards.question: Jesus wants them to know the Son of Man has authority on the earth to do something. What is it?
Jesus turns to the paralyzed man and tells him to get up, pick up his ___ and go home.

cards.text: And IMMEDIATELY the man stands up in front of them and picks up what he'd been lying on. He came in through the ROOF, and he goes home on his own two feet.

cards.question: The man who couldn't walk is heading home. What is he doing on the way?
Everyone who saw the paralyzed man walk is amazed and glorifies God too.

cards.text: They're filled with awe and say, “We have seen remarkable things today.” Remarkable? Friend, a man came down through the ceiling and walked home. I'd need to sit down for a WEEK.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 5 quotes "Lord, if You are willing.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 11 quotes "Who can forgive sins but ___ alone?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: 'Jesus is in one of the towns…', 'Not a patch here and there.', 'COVERED.' and 'When he sees Jesus…'. The opening card can have at most 3.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences ('Jesus reaches out…', 'TOUCHES him!', 'I bet that man…'). Story cards after the opening card can have at most 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences ('Jesus said don't tell anyone.', 'And the news…', 'Friend, there is no such thing…'). Story cards after the opening card can have at most 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card retells Jesus' instruction 'don't tell anyone' from Luke 5:14 but cites only Luke 5:15. The citation should be Luke 5:14-15.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The joke 'there is no such thing as "just between us"' says the healed man told people and that this is how the news spread. Luke 5:15 says only that the news about Jesus spread all the more. It never says how the news spread or that the man told anyone.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences ('Friend, if the parking lot's full…', 'These men went through the ROOF.', 'And Jesus sees it all.'). Story cards after the opening card can have at most 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Earlier cards give away the answer 'mat' before this card asks for it. Card 3 says the men are 'carrying a paralyzed man on a mat', and card 6 says they 'lower the paralyzed man on his mat'.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The question asks what the man is doing on his way home. The wrong answer 'Heading to the temple' is a different destination, not something he does on the way home, so it isn't the same kind of thing as the other answers. The wrong answer 'Telling the Pharisees' isn't believable either, because the Pharisees are back at the house, not on his way home. Both wrong answers make the right one stand out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This story card has 4 sentences (the awe and quote sentence, 'Remarkable?', 'Friend, a man came down…', 'I'd need to sit down…'). Story cards after the opening card can have at most 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
